title: Cost Control Console: recommendation cards, config diff preview, and safe apply + rollback audit trail
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Deliver a cohesive Console UX in Optimize that surfaces automated batching/caching recommendations as actionable cards, shows deterministic config diffs before apply, and provides a searchable apply history with a verifiable audit trail and safe rollback flow. This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout and observability for the initial end-to-end experience.
background: Customers running high-throughput LLM workloads can lower token costs by tuning batching and prefix/KV caching. We already compute recommendations server-side (engine prototype ENG-2891), but customers lack an easy, auditable path to preview and apply those changes to serving configs. Engineering needs a clear UI contract and UX flow to minimize accidental regressions and to enable rollbacks with context.
goals: Provide an at-a-glance recommendation card UI that summarizes expected cost and latency impact and confidence score
Allow users to preview a deterministic diff between current runtime config and proposed changes before applying
Implement a safe apply workflow: dry-run option, canary apply to a fraction of traffic, timed automatic rollback on regression, and manual rollback from console
Store every apply/rollback as an immutable audit record with operator, timestamp, rationale, linked evals and GitHub PRs
Emit telemetry events and cost/latency observability for applied changes to verify impact
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display: rule name, targeted service/model, estimated monthly savings (USD), expected tail-latency impact (+/- ms), confidence score (low/med/high) and link to 'why' explainer
Clicking a card opens a diff preview modal showing current vs. proposed YAML with inline highlights and ability to toggle 'rendered' human-friendly view
Apply flow requires: operator confirmation, optional free-text rationale, selection of deployment scope (single route / model / org), and canary percentage slider (0-100)
All applies generate an audit entry accessible in Optimize -> Activity with filters (operator, date range, model, change type) and detail view linking to telemetry and eval snapshots
Rollback button in audit entry performs one-click rollback to the previous active config and records the operator, time and reason
Dry-run API returns a deterministic preflight report and score; actual apply API supports staged rollout and returns a job id for status polling

Telemetry events emitted: optimize.recommendation.view, optimize.recommendation.apply.start, optimize.recommendation.apply.complete, optimize.recommendation.rollback, optimize.recommendation.apply.fail
Feature is behind Console feature-flag 'optimize_safe_apply' and respects RBAC so only users with 'config.apply' can execute applies/rollbacks
Security review completed and audit entries meet retention and export requirements for compliance (CSV/JSON download)
ui_notes: Recommendation card should use 3-tier confidence color system and show estimated savings band rather than single point estimate
Diff preview must support side-by-side and inline modes and render KV cache and batching params prominently
When canary is selected, show simulated traffic split and expected warm-up time for KV cache
Error states: show clear remediation steps and link to runbook when apply fails due to incompatible model variant or insufficient capacity
api_contract: GET /v1/optimize/recommendations?model=<id>&route=<id> => list of recommendation objects (id, type, estimated_savings_usd, confidence, patch_yaml, rationale_url)
POST /v1/optimize/apply => body: { recommendation_id, scope, canary_pct, dry_run(bool), rationale } returns { job_id, preflight_report_url }
POST /v1/optimize/rollback => body: { applied_config_id, reason } returns { rollback_job_id }
engineering_notes: ENG-2891 implements server-side recommendation generator; must extend response to include patch_yaml and confidence_band
ENG-3044 implements canary routing and staged rollout engine; coordinate on job id contract and status polling
Ensure apply/rollback operations are idempotent and include optimistic locking on config version
Storage: audit entries written to immutable audit-store; include links to telemetry snapshot and evaluation artifacts
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only behind feature flag 'optimize_safe_apply' with selected accounts (2 SRE + 3 customers) - 2 weeks
Beta: enable for enterprise customers with 'config.apply' RBAC enabled - 4 weeks
GA: on by default for all accounts with opt-out - tied to console-2026.03 release
observability: Dashboards: per-apply job success rate, average time-to-apply, average rollback latency, mean cost delta post-apply
Alerting: apply.fail rate > 5% over 1h triggers PagerDuty to infra team; rollback rate > 2% over 24h triggers review
Correlation: link apply job to model serving traces and per-token cost breakdown
security_and_compliance: Audit entries must store operator identity (SSO), IP, request-id and signed checksum of config blob
Allow export of audit history for compliance reviews in CSV with anonymization option
Feature must respect org-level data residency; audit-store writes should route to customer VPC when in private deployment
open_questions: What is the canonical schema for patch_yaml? (full config vs. minimal delta)
What retention window for audit entries is required by Compliance? default 1 year vs. configurable
Should Apply support auto-heal (auto-rollback) thresholds by default, and if so what are sensible defaults?
